The founder is closely involved at this stage, which gives you senior attention, but the operating model is designed so that work can continue without them: one named Engagement Lead per engagement, documented standards and decision rules, client access granted to named individuals through company-controlled arrangements, and contractors and associates working within Vitalos systems. Over time, authority moves from the founder to engagement, technical and practice leaders. If continuity matters especially for your engagement, raise it and Vitalos will show you how it is covered.

entries.question: Why not hire an in-house team instead?
entries.shortAnswer: Building your own team gives you long-term ownership and institutional knowledge, and for permanent core capability it is often right. It is also slow, specialist skills are hard to recruit and capacity is fixed. Vitalos gives you flexible specialist capability now and can transfer knowledge so your own team can take over.
entries.fullAnswer: The choice is rarely all or nothing. Many organisations use Vitalos for work that needs specialist skills or more capacity than their team has, such as a modernisation programme, an AI implementation or a rescue, while they hire for the long term. Vitalos documents its work, can work in your tools, and plans handover from the start, so you are not left dependent on an outside firm. If the honest answer is that you should hire rather than buy services, Vitalos will tell you so.

entries.question: Why not use a big systems integrator?
entries.shortAnswer: A large systems integrator brings brand, scale and procurement familiarity, and for very large programmes that can be the right choice. It often also means higher overhead and more layers between you and the people delivering. Vitalos offers senior involvement, faster decisions and engineering accountability without that overhead.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos is not trying to look like a global integrator, and it will not claim scale it does not have. It is designed for organisations that want senior people close to the problem, one accountable lead, advice and engineering in the same team, and commercial sense. It keeps the disciplines that reduce risk, such as lifecycle gates, security and quality controls, written scope and documented handover, without enterprise ceremony that adds cost but not safety. Where your programme needs scale or specialist capability that Vitalos lacks, it will say so.

entries.question: What if the project fails?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos structures work so problems surface early and investment follows evidence. Engagements are staged with decision gates, risks are reported plainly every week, changes go through change control, and quality gates cannot be skipped to protect a date. If Vitalos misses something it owns it openly, and your contract sets out the remedies.
entries.fullAnswer: Many failures start before delivery, with an unclear problem or an unrealistic plan, so Vitalos insists on discovery where uncertainty is material and declines work that depends on impossible dates or unsafe shortcuts. During delivery, an escalation culture means bad news travels fast and decisions are made with you. If the evidence says a project should stop, change direction or change scope, Vitalos will say so rather than keep spending your money. Contracts give you warranty, defect correction, termination and exit rights, so that even in the worst case you keep what you have paid for.

entries.question: Can Vitalos work with our existing supplier?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Vitalos can work alongside your existing suppliers and internal teams, provided responsibilities are clear. That might mean taking on a specific workstream, integrating with a system another supplier runs, assessing a platform independently, or taking over from a supplier through a structured handover and takeover assessment.
entries.fullAnswer: The key is a written responsibility model: who owns which system, decisions, risks and support, and how issues are escalated between suppliers. Vitalos can work in your existing tools, such as your ticketing or delivery systems, and follow agreed standards. Where Vitalos takes over from a supplier, it assesses ownership, access, code, security, deployment and documentation first, and will not accept service levels for a system it does not yet understand. Independent assessments state their findings factually and with evidence, so you can discuss them with your supplier.

entries.question: Aren't you just another web or AI agency?
entries.shortAnswer: No. Vitalos is a technology consulting, engineering and digital transformation firm. It leads with your business problem rather than a technology, connects advice to production engineering and ongoing operation, and declines routine brochure-website work. AI is used where it creates measurable value, inside real workflows and governance, not as a standalone chatbot.
entries.fullAnswer: Agencies often sell a deliverable: a website, an app or an AI demonstration. Vitalos sells outcomes and stays accountable for them: it decides with you what should change, engineers it to production standards, and can operate and improve it afterwards. Its delivery model includes architecture decisions, security and quality gates, documentation and service transition, and these disciplines are part of every Vitalos production engagement. Vitalos does build web platforms and AI solutions, but as part of a broader transformation, not as commodity work.

entries.question: Can a small firm handle work for a large organisation?
entries.shortAnswer: A small firm can handle work for a large organisation when the scope is right. Vitalos takes on suitable enterprise work selectively, commits only the capacity it can credibly provide, and uses qualified partners where specialist depth is needed. It will tell you plainly if your programme needs more scale than it can deliver.
entries.fullAnswer: Larger organisations bring longer procurement, security questionnaires, broader contract terms and higher evidence requirements. Vitalos prepares for these deliberately, through the Trust Centre, a procurement evidence route, a contract stack designed for enterprise negotiation and a staged certification roadmap, and it prices the cost of enterprise procurement honestly rather than absorbing it. Often the best fit is a bounded, high-value piece of work, such as an assessment, a rescue or a defined AI implementation, where senior attention matters more than headcount.

entries.question: Will Vitalos tell us if we don't need its services?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. If an assessment shows you should not invest, should wait, should fix something simpler first, or should use another supplier or your own team, Vitalos will say so. It recommends the next logical step based on genuine need, not unrelated services, and does not under-scope work to win larger contracts later.
entries.fullAnswer: Long-term trust is worth more than one sale. Vitalos's commercial rules forbid forced upselling and recommending unnecessary work, and its assessments are designed to be useful even if you never buy anything else. "Not yet" and "not us" are legitimate conclusions. Account growth at Vitalos is meant to come from value delivered, measured by outcomes and relationship depth rather than the number of services sold. Proposals for follow-on work explain why the work is needed and what evidence supports it.

entries.question: What happens to our system if Vitalos stops trading?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos designs engagements so that you are not exposed if it disappears. For long-lived systems it prefers production cloud, domain and other strategic accounts to be owned by you, and code, documentation and runbooks to be handed over as the work proceeds, not only at the end.
entries.fullAnswer: The measures that prevent lock-in also protect you against supplier failure. Bespoke deliverables can be assigned to you once paid for, and you receive a perpetual licence for any embedded Vitalos components, so you can keep using and changing what you have. Documentation is a required deliverable, so another competent team could take over. Where a managed service relies on accounts Vitalos holds, the contract defines how they transfer to you. If supplier resilience matters in your procurement, ask for the evidence you need through the procurement route.

entries.question: Which industries does Vitalos focus on?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos focuses on four launch sectors: Health & Care; Retail, Commerce & Consumer; Operations, Industry & Logistics; and Growth & Technology. Growth & Technology is a selective proposition for startups, scale-ups and technology businesses rather than a claim of deep sector specialism.
entries.fullAnswer: Focusing on a few sectors lets Vitalos build repeatable domain knowledge, language, reusable accelerators and relevant proof faster than spreading across every market. The three operational sectors share common problems: manual workflows, fragmented systems, data that does not support decisions and pressure to adopt AI responsibly. Growth & Technology covers product engineering, architecture, platform modernisation, AI implementation and engineering rescue where the commercial fit is strong. Vitalos does not create sector pages it cannot support with useful knowledge or proof, and new sectors are added only when they are earned through work, people or serious research.

entries.question: Do you work with organisations outside these sectors?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes, selectively. The sector focus guides where Vitalos builds depth and proof, but the problems it solves, such as manual operations, legacy systems, fragmented data and AI adoption, appear across many industries. Vitalos takes on work in other sectors when the problem fits and it can deliver credibly.
entries.fullAnswer: What matters most is the problem, the sponsor and whether Vitalos can deliver responsibly. If your sector has specialist regulation, assurance or domain requirements that Vitalos cannot meet itself, it will say so and may propose working alongside a qualified specialist under a clear responsibility model. Vitalos does not claim deep expertise in sectors where it has not developed it, so you will get an honest view of what Vitalos already understands about your industry and what it would need to learn from your people during discovery.

entries.question: What does Vitalos do for health and care organisations?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos helps healthcare providers, social care organisations and health-tech and care-tech businesses modernise operational workflows and scheduling, build digital services and portals, connect records and data flows, improve reporting and apply compliance-aware AI with human oversight, while managing privacy, accessibility, safety and trust.
entries.fullAnswer: Health and care operations depend on workflows, scheduling, records and data flows that shape how staff spend their time, and on digital services that patients, service users and staff can actually use. Vitalos focuses on reducing administrative burden, connecting systems, improving operational intelligence and designing accessible services. Privacy, security, safety and accessibility are built into discovery and delivery rather than reviewed at the end. Work that touches clinical decisions or regulated compliance needs specialist clinical, legal or accredited assurance alongside technology delivery, and Vitalos is clear about where its own role ends.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss a health & care challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Does Vitalos have an NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT) submission?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos has not yet completed an NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit submission. The DSPT applies to organisations with access to NHS patient data and systems, so Vitalos will complete it when an engagement gives it that access, and will state its status honestly before contracting.
entries.fullAnswer: The NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit is how organisations with access to NHS patient data and systems show they meet the National Data Guardian's data security standards. The 2026–27 version was released in September 2026 and is aligned to the Cyber Assessment Framework. Vitalos's approach is to build the underlying controls first and complete the toolkit when a concrete NHS engagement with data or system access makes it applicable. If your project would give Vitalos access to NHS patient data or systems, raise it early, because DSPT completion and related assurance then become part of the plan and the timetable.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss a health & care challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: How does Vitalos handle patient and service-user data and information governance?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos treats health and care data as high risk. Purposes, access, retention and deletion are made explicit, a data protection impact assessment is used for higher-risk processing, a data processing agreement is put in place where Vitalos processes data for you, and legal interpretation is escalated to qualified advisers.
entries.fullAnswer: Information governance starts before any data is shared. Vitalos agrees with you whether it is acting as a processor on your instructions, what data is needed and why, who can access it, where it is stored and processed, and how long it is kept. Highly sensitive personal data falls into the restricted class of the Vitalos data classification model, which means need-to-know access, strong authentication, restricted sharing and dedicated storage. Prototypes and testing use synthetic or minimised data wherever possible. If an engagement would give Vitalos access to NHS patient data or systems, the NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit is planned into the work.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss a health & care challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Can AI be used safely in health and care settings?
entries.shortAnswer: AI can be used safely in health and care within the right limits. Vitalos focuses on compliance-aware AI in administrative and operational workflows, with human oversight wherever decisions affect people. Anything that could influence clinical decisions needs qualified clinical assurance alongside the engineering, and Vitalos raises that early.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos's focus is AI that reduces administrative effort, such as scheduling, document handling and reporting, where outputs can be checked and errors contained. Vitalos applies its standard AI controls: a defined purpose, evaluation against agreed criteria, human review where risk warrants it, bounded permissions for any agent, monitoring once live, and clear accountability for final decisions. Deterministic automation is used first where it is more reliable. Vitalos does not present AI as a replacement for clinical judgement, and it will tell you if a proposed use needs regulatory or clinical safety assessment beyond its competence.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss a health & care challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What does Vitalos do for retail, commerce and consumer businesses?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos helps retailers, e-commerce businesses, wholesalers, distributors, consumer brands, and food and hospitality operators modernise commerce platforms, integrate inventory and order systems, improve the customer experience, automate the operations behind the storefront, and build analytics, forecasting and AI-enabled customer service on data the business can rely on.
entries.fullAnswer: In retail and commerce, customer experience, merchandising and fulfilment have to work together across online and operational systems, and inventory, orders and customer data often sit in separate platforms that must stay in step. Vitalos connects those systems, redesigns the customer journey together with the operations behind it, and builds the data foundation that forecasting and AI depend on. Changes to trading systems are released with validation, release control and rollback planned to protect live trading. Typical starting points are Customer Experience Transformation, Systems Integration, Data & BI Modernisation or an AI Opportunity Assessment.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss a commerce challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Can Vitalos connect our e-commerce platform with our inventory and order systems?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes, this is a core use of the Systems Integration offer. Vitalos maps the systems, data and ownership involved, then builds integrations that keep stock, orders and customer data in step, with monitoring and alerts for failures and documented runbooks for your team.
entries.fullAnswer: Disconnected commerce systems lead to oversold stock, delayed orders, manual reconciliation and a poor customer experience. Vitalos treats each data flow as a business process: who owns it, what it must guarantee and what should happen when something fails. Integrations are tested for retries, duplicate prevention and dependence on external services before they carry live orders. Vitalos does not claim certified partner status with specific commerce platforms; it works through their interfaces and will tell you early if a platform's limits or terms affect what is possible.

entries.question: How do you avoid disrupting trading when you change our commerce systems?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos protects live trading with controlled release practice. Changes move through test and staging environments, are validated for function and performance, and are released with a rollback plan and post-release checks. Higher-risk releases need your approval as well as Vitalos's before they go live.
entries.fullAnswer: A deployment that succeeds technically can still disrupt trading if data migration, configuration or monitoring is wrong. Vitalos's release standard covers migration, configuration, observability, support ownership, rollback and recovery, user communication and post-release verification. A deadline is not approval to skip peer review, validation, backup or rollback planning. If the safe release path cannot be completed, the risk is escalated and the release decision is made explicitly and on record, rather than being taken quietly under time pressure. After each material release, post-release checks confirm that orders, stock and payments are flowing as expected.

entries.question: What does Vitalos do for operations, industry and logistics businesses?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos helps manufacturers, logistics and supply chain operators, engineering businesses, field-service organisations and other operationally intensive firms digitise manual processes, integrate the systems they depend on, build operational dashboards and mobile field tools, replace ageing legacy systems and apply AI-assisted operations on data that managers can rely on.
entries.fullAnswer: Operationally intensive businesses often still run critical processes on manual steps and disconnected tools, and field, warehouse and fleet data is only useful when it reaches the people planning and running operations. Vitalos redesigns workflows, connects systems, and builds the operational intelligence and forecasting that sit on top. Operational systems have to keep working while they are improved, so resilience, recovery and rollback planning are matched to how critical each system is. Typical starting points are a Digital Transformation Discovery, Systems Integration, Business Process Automation or a Technology Health Assessment.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss an operations challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Can Vitalos build tools for field teams, warehouses or fleets?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Vitalos designs and builds mobile and field tools and connects the data they produce to planning and operations. Tools are designed with the people who use them in real operating conditions, and the data flows into dashboards and decision systems so managers can see what is happening without chasing updates.
entries.fullAnswer: Field and warehouse tools fail when they are designed in an office for ideal conditions. The Vitalos Experience practice researches how the work is actually done, including connectivity, devices and time pressure, and Engineering builds tools that fit those conditions. Integration with your existing systems means data is entered once and reaches the people who need it. Where AI adds value, for example in forecasting or asset and process intelligence, it is built on the integrated data and evaluated like any other production AI. Vitalos does not claim previous field-tool deployments it cannot evidence.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss an operations challenge / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Can Vitalos give us reliable, up-to-date visibility of our operations?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes, that is the purpose of operational dashboards and decision systems built on integrated data. Vitalos connects the systems that hold your operational data, agrees definitions for the measures that matter, monitors data freshness and quality, and builds reporting your managers can trust.
entries.fullAnswer: Visibility fails when figures arrive late, disagree between reports or depend on someone's spreadsheet. Vitalos starts with the decisions managers need to make, then works back to the data required. Each important measure gets a documented business definition and an owner. Pipelines are monitored for failure and freshness, so stale data is flagged rather than shown as if it were current. Where it adds value, forecasting or AI-assisted decision support is built on that foundation. Typical routes are Data & BI Modernisation or Systems Integration, often after a short discovery.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Data & BI Modernisation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Does Vitalos work with startups and scale-ups?
entries.shortAnswer: Selectively. Vitalos supports startups, scale-ups and technology businesses with architecture, product engineering, platform modernisation, AI implementation and engineering rescue where the commercial fit is strong. Growth & Technology is a selective proposition, not a low-cost MVP service or a claim of deep sector specialism.
entries.fullAnswer: The best fit is a technology business with a capable team that needs specialist capacity for a major build or modernisation, or a product that has stalled or become hard to maintain and needs rescue before it can grow. Vitalos brings the same delivery standards it applies to larger clients: recorded architecture decisions, tested increments, security by design and documentation your team can work with. Budgets and stability vary in early-stage companies, so Vitalos qualifies these opportunities carefully, and it does not compete on the lowest price for minimum viable products.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Discuss a product or platform / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What does Vitalos publish in Insights?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Insights publishes practical thinking for business and technology leaders: executive briefings, insight articles, engineering notes, guides and research. Topics include AI and agents, digital transformation, software and platforms, data, cloud and reliability, experience and commerce, and the three operational sectors Vitalos focuses on.
entries.fullAnswer: Each format has a job. Executive briefings are short and decision-oriented. Insight articles and points of view take a clear, evidence-based position. Engineering notes show practitioner-level technical judgement. Guides give a structured approach you can use. Research reports add original data when Vitalos has it. Case-derived insights extract lessons from real delivery without duplicating case studies. Vitalos aims for useful pieces that leaders and engineers save and share, rather than high volumes of generic trend articles, and it does not publish invented statistics.

entries.question: Who writes Vitalos Insights, and is it written by AI?
entries.shortAnswer: Every substantive Vitalos Insight has a named human author who is accountable for its accuracy and judgement. AI may help with research, structure or editing, but Vitalos does not publish unreviewed machine-generated thought leadership, and claims, citations and figures are checked before anything is published.
entries.fullAnswer: Named authorship matters because you should know whose judgement you are reading and be able to see their role and related work. Institutional pieces may be published under the Vitalos name, but anonymous marketing-team thought leadership is not the norm. Before publication, claims, citations, screenshots and external links are reviewed, and publication and update dates are shown on every article. Over time, Vitalos intends Insights to carry several expert voices across its practices, not just the founder's. Each author has a profile showing their role and related work.

entries.question: How often does Vitalos publish?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos aims to publish a substantive insight, engineering note or executive briefing about every two weeks once Insights is established, but quality comes first. Vitalos would rather publish less often than release weak material to keep up a schedule, and it does not launch sections that say coming soon.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos is building an initial body of useful content before making Insights a main destination, rather than opening an empty section. Pieces are tied to the problems clients actually face: production AI, modernisation, operations, data and the target sectors. Larger research pieces, webinars and roundtables follow at a slower pace, and only when there is real substance to share. Every article shows its publication and update dates, so you can judge how current it is before relying on it. Older pieces are updated or retired when they stop being accurate.

entries.question: What is Vitalos Labs?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Labs is the research and technical proof capability of Vitalos, separate from its five practices. It builds reference architectures, prototypes, evaluation methods, reusable engineering accelerators and, occasionally, product candidates. Labs shows how Vitalos thinks and builds before many client case studies exist, and every asset is labelled with its maturity.
entries.fullAnswer: Labs exists to develop reusable capability, explore relevant technology before it becomes mainstream, demonstrate engineering judgement and test product ideas that emerge from repeated client problems. It does not chase every new model or framework, build products without customers, or rebrand unfinished internal tools as software products. Labs work is deliberately kept small and evidence-led, with an owner, a budget and stop criteria for each initiative, so it strengthens the consulting business rather than distracting from it. Most Labs ideas are paused or stopped before they become products, and that is deliberate.

entries.question: Are Labs projects products we can buy?
entries.shortAnswer: Most Vitalos Labs assets are not products you can buy. They are research, concepts, prototypes or accelerators, each labelled so that a prototype is never mistaken for a supported product. An asset becomes a product only with repeated demand, a dedicated owner, a support and security model and credible economics.
entries.fullAnswer: Labs maturity runs from Research through Concept, Prototype and Accelerator to Beta and, rarely, Production product. Accelerators are reusable components or methods that Vitalos uses in client delivery, and they can be embedded in your solution under licence. A Beta has real users with explicit limitations. A Production product has a separate commercial model, support arrangements and terms. If a Labs asset interests you, ask about it: it may speed up your engagement as an accelerator, or Vitalos may be looking for design partners to test it further.

entries.question: Are Labs demonstrations based on client work?
entries.shortAnswer: No. Labs assets are kept separate from client work. Client confidential information and client-owned IP are never turned into Labs assets without rights and permission, and Labs concepts are never presented as client deployments. Real client outcomes appear only in the Work section, with the client's permission.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos is strict about the line between Labs and Work, because blurring it would mislead you. Labs assets state what exists, what was tested and what remains unknown, with known limitations shown. They use synthetic or non-sensitive data by default and are published only after review for technical soundness, safety and maintainability. Repeated client problems can inspire Labs research, but only general, non-confidential learning is reused, and always within the IP and confidentiality terms of each client contract. Client names never appear in Labs material.

entries.question: What do the Labs maturity labels mean?
entries.shortAnswer: Each Labs asset carries one label. Research means exploration or analysis, not a product. Concept means a defined idea with limited implementation. Prototype means a working proof of feasibility. Accelerator means a reusable delivery component. Beta or Pilot means limited use with explicit constraints. Production product means a separately supported commercial product.
entries.fullAnswer: The labels tell you how much weight to put on an asset. A Research note or Concept can show how Vitalos thinks about a problem, but it does not imply working software. A Prototype shows that something can work in a test context, with its limitations stated. An Accelerator is used in real delivery, but it does not come with independent product service levels. Only a Production product carries normal product claims, support and commercial terms. Labels are shown prominently on every asset page, and stale experiments are retired rather than left on display.

entries.question: Can we work with Vitalos Labs as a design partner?
entries.shortAnswer: Organisations can work with Vitalos Labs as design partners when a Labs asset is moving towards becoming a product. Design partners help shape it in return for influence, early access or preferential terms, under a written agreement covering confidentiality, IP, data and security boundaries, support limits and commitments on both sides.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos prefers design partners and paid pilots to speculative large builds, and looks for at least two or three independent organisations before treating a problem as broadly repeatable. Design partners are not unpaid product managers, and one partner's needs will not turn the product into bespoke consulting. Prototypes used in design partnerships rely on synthetic or controlled data by default, and their limitations are stated plainly. If you have a problem that a Labs asset might address, Talk to Vitalos.

entries.question: Who owns the IP created in Vitalos Labs?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos owns the IP created in Vitalos Labs. Labs research, prototypes, accelerators and product IP remain Vitalos Background IP unless a funded collaboration agreement says otherwise. Where a Labs accelerator is used in your project, you receive a licence to use it in your deliverable, and your own data, content and configuration remain yours.
entries.fullAnswer: Separating Labs IP from client work protects both sides. Client agreements are written so that using a Vitalos accelerator during delivery does not accidentally transfer it, and so that client-funded bespoke features are treated as your foreground deliverables under the statement of work. When a Labs asset becomes a commercial product, it moves onto separate product terms, a data processing agreement and service levels rather than being sold through consultancy contracts. External datasets, models and components used in Labs keep their own licence terms.

entries.question: What operational responsibilities does a Vitalos managed service take on?
entries.shortAnswer: A Vitalos managed service takes defined responsibility for a live system within an agreed boundary. Depending on the service, it covers monitoring and alerting, incident triage and response, defect fixes, security and dependency maintenance, release management, reliability, backup checks, supplier monitoring, service reporting and continuous improvement.
entries.fullAnswer: Managed services come in several forms: Application Care for maintenance and support, retained engineering capacity, platform and cloud operations, continuous product improvement, Managed AI and Managed Data. Every service starts with a formal transition that defines the service boundary, support contacts, escalation, monitoring, runbooks, access, maintenance responsibilities, known exceptions and any initial remediation. Monthly service reviews cover incidents, backlog, risks and improvements. The aim is a system that keeps improving, not passive ticket handling, and the service schedule makes clear what is included and what is quoted separately.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Managed Engineering & Application Care / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Does Vitalos provide 24/7 support?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos does not provide 24/7 support as a standard service. It does not promise round-the-clock support, security monitoring or incident response unless the rota, tooling and economics to deliver it are in place and written into your contract. If your system needs 24/7 cover, Vitalos will tell you plainly what it can provide.
entries.fullAnswer: Promising 24/7 support without the people and processes to deliver it would put your service at risk. Vitalos managed services are designed around agreed service hours, severity definitions and escalation routes. For critical systems that need cover outside those hours, the options can be discussed openly, such as working alongside your own on-call team or a specialist provider for continuous monitoring. Having people in several time zones does not by itself create genuine round-the-clock capability, and Vitalos will not imply that it does.

entries.question: How does Vitalos monitor live systems?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos monitors live systems through logs, metrics, traces and alerts designed around user and business impact, not just infrastructure health. Critical journeys and integrations are watched, alerts go to a named owner, and pipeline failures or stale data are flagged before users discover them.
entries.fullAnswer: Observability is designed in during build, so systems Vitalos delivers expose enough information to show whether critical services are working. For inherited systems, the takeover assessment checks existing monitoring, logs and alerts, and gaps go into the transition plan. An alert without an owner is not a control, so every alert has someone responsible for responding and an escalation path. Monitoring data also feeds monthly service reviews, highlighting reliability and incident trends, cost and efficiency opportunities, and places where automation could prevent repeat problems.

entries.question: What happens when there is an incident?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos classifies incidents by severity, from SEV-1 critical to SEV-4 low. A critical incident means immediate escalation, an incident lead, frequent updates to you and recovery first. Lower severities get defined ownership and update rhythms. Every significant incident ends with a review of its root cause and lessons learned.
entries.fullAnswer: The severity model keeps responses proportionate. SEV-1 covers major outages, serious security or data events and severe business impact. SEV-2 covers significant degradation or a high-impact defect with limited workaround, handled with rapid ownership and prioritised remediation. SEV-3 covers contained issues handled through normal prioritisation, and SEV-4 covers minor issues for the backlog. Each incident is recorded with its impact, timeline, actions and root cause. Communication duties to you, and any regulator or data-subject notifications, are agreed in your contract so that roles are clear before anything goes wrong.

entries.question: Will Vitalos support a system it did not build?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos supports systems it did not build, but only after a takeover assessment. It reviews ownership and access, architecture, code, security, data, operations, documentation and your service expectations first. The outcome may be acceptance as it is, acceptance with a remediation plan, a rescue first, or a decline.
entries.fullAnswer: Supporting systems built by others is valuable, but it can import unknown risk, so acceptance is never automatic. The assessment is paid because it does real work: identifying technical debt, undocumented dependencies, access problems, security weaknesses and immediate fixes. Material unknowns become an assessment or transition engagement before any service level is accepted. Vitalos declines where the risk, access, legality, capability gap or commercial model makes responsible support impossible. The Vitalos rule is that "we will support it" is an operational commitment, not a sales phrase.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Managed Engineering & Application Care / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: How do we leave a Vitalos managed service?
entries.shortAnswer: Exit is designed into every Vitalos managed service from the start. Your contract sets the notice period and transition assistance, and the exit process covers code and documentation, runbooks, credentials, data return or deletion, account and licence transfers, knowledge-transfer sessions and shutdown of any Vitalos-held services.
entries.fullAnswer: You should be able to move a service to your own team or another provider without disruption. Vitalos keeps documentation current during the service, so exit does not depend on reconstructing knowledge at the last minute. Where Vitalos owns operational accounts or platforms as part of the service, the contract defines how they are transferred. Client-owned deliverables are not withheld after payment. Legitimate unpaid fees, Vitalos Background IP and licensed product rights remain protected through the contract, but there is no artificial technical lock-in.

entries.question: Is a managed service just ticket handling?
entries.shortAnswer: No. Each Vitalos managed service keeps an improvement backlog covering reliability, automation, cost, security, user friction and product evolution. Monthly service reviews look at incidents, risks and improvements, and strategic accounts also have periodic value reviews focused on business outcomes rather than ticket counts.
entries.fullAnswer: Live systems should keep getting better, not just stay up. Vitalos compares the live system against business outcomes, operational data, incidents, user behaviour, cost and technical debt, and proposes the next most valuable changes. Improvement work is planned within the agreed capacity, or scoped separately if it goes beyond the service boundary. Vitalos measures managed services by client outcomes and reliability first; the number of tickets closed or lines of code written is not treated as evidence of value. Improvement priorities are agreed with you at each service review.

entries.question: Does Vitalos offer Managed AI?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Managed AI operates, evaluates and improves AI capabilities in production under agreed controls. It covers monitoring of quality, cost and latency, periodic re-evaluation as models, prompts and data change, controlled model and provider updates, incident handling and governance support, so live AI keeps behaving as intended.
entries.fullAnswer: AI systems change even when your code does not: providers update models, data drifts and usage patterns shift. Managed AI is the final stage of the Vitalos AI journey, AI Opportunity Assessment > Prototype > Production > Managed AI, and keeps the capability within the quality and risk limits agreed at launch. It includes evaluation runs, monitoring of error, escalation and cost measures, optimisation of cost and quality, and change management for model or provider updates made for security, availability, cost or quality reasons. Managed Data applies the same operational discipline to data pipelines and analytics.

entries.question: What is a Digital Transformation Discovery, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: A Digital Transformation Discovery is a bounded, normally fixed-fee engagement for leaders who know parts of the business need modernising but need a coherent plan. Vitalos maps the current state, defines the future state with you and produces a prioritised roadmap, which usually becomes an implementation programme.
entries.fullAnswer: It suits organisations where transformation uncertainty is high: several departments or systems are affected, process redesign is needed, architecture or integration decisions are unresolved, requirements are contested, or the investment is large enough that you need evidence before committing. It is also the right start when building straight away would be irresponsible because of risk, regulation or integration complexity. Vitalos Consulting leads the work, with Experience, Engineering and AI & Data specialists joining as needed under one Engagement Lead. The resulting roadmap can be delivered as an implementation programme across Engineering, AI & Data or Experience, by Vitalos or by another team.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Digital Transformation Discovery / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for a Digital Transformation Discovery, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a named sponsor, a decision-maker for outcomes and priorities, and access to the people, processes, systems and data in scope. You receive a current-state analysis, a process and system map, pain points, a future-state vision, prioritised initiatives and a roadmap with dependencies and sequence.
entries.fullAnswer: Discovery only works if Vitalos can see how the business really operates, so we ask for workshop time with process owners and, where relevant, users, plus existing documentation and data. We also need timely decisions on outcomes and priorities so the roadmap reflects what you actually want. The outputs are designed to be acted on. The roadmap names priorities, sequencing, dependencies, risks and decision points, and where a first phase is clear enough it is defined so that it can be estimated and contracted. Implementation of the roadmap is scoped as its own engagement and is not included in the discovery fee.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Digital Transformation Discovery / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is a Technology Health Assessment, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: A Technology Health Assessment is a fixed-fee, independent review of a platform or technology estate. It suits leaders who need to know what is wrong, risky or holding their systems back before deciding whether to modernise, rescue, replace or hand the system to a managed service.
entries.fullAnswer: Typical triggers are risky releases, rising incidents, dependence on one developer or a slow supplier, due diligence, a customer or regulator asking for assurance, or a growth plan the current systems may not support. Vitalos Consulting and Engineering review architecture, code and technical debt, security and reliability, and performance risks, then turn the findings into a prioritised remediation plan. You can act on the plan with Vitalos, with another supplier or with your own team. The natural next steps are Application Modernisation, Engineering Rescue or Managed Engineering & Application Care, depending on what the assessment finds.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Technology Health Assessment / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for a Technology Health Assessment, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a named sponsor, read-only access to code, infrastructure, deployment pipelines, documentation and monitoring, and time with technical and business owners. You receive an architecture review, a technical debt assessment, security and reliability observations, performance risks and a prioritised remediation plan.
entries.fullAnswer: Read-only access is usually enough, because the assessment examines the system rather than changing it. Supplier contacts and incident history help us understand where problems have come from. The findings are written for technical and business readers alike, so leadership can see where the real risks and costs sit and what to fix first. Two limits are worth stating plainly. The security observations are not a penetration test, a formal audit or a certification. And the remediation work itself is scoped separately, so you are free to choose who carries it out.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Technology Health Assessment / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is an AI Opportunity Assessment, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: An AI Opportunity Assessment is the fixed-fee first step of the Vitalos AI journey. It identifies and ranks viable AI use cases by value, feasibility, data readiness and risk. It suits leadership teams who know AI matters but do not yet know where it would pay off safely.
entries.fullAnswer: Common triggers are board or investor pressure for an AI plan, a stalled pilot, a competitor visibly automating, or one obviously manual and costly process. Vitalos Consulting and AI & Data examine your business processes, opportunity value, data readiness, systems and integration, security and privacy, Responsible AI and operating readiness. The result is a ranked set of opportunities grounded in your real processes and data, with an honest view of what is not ready. The natural next step is an AI Prototype Sprint for the strongest use case, following AI Opportunity Assessment > Prototype > Production > Managed AI. A "not yet" answer is also legitimate.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Opportunity Assessment / Start an AI Opportunity Assessment

entries.question: What do we need to provide for an AI Opportunity Assessment, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a named sponsor, time with the people who own the processes in scope, and a view of the data that candidate use cases would rely on. You receive prioritised AI use cases, a feasibility and risk assessment, readiness findings, prototype recommendations, an adoption roadmap and an executive readout.
entries.fullAnswer: The assessment runs through four steps: discover, evaluate, prioritise and recommend. Use cases are scored on value, feasibility, data readiness and risk, with the reasoning shown so you can challenge the ranking. Readiness covers data, systems, skills, governance and Responsible AI considerations. The recommended first move is normally a scoped prototype for the single best opportunity, including what proven would look like. Building or deploying AI is not included; that starts with an AI Prototype Sprint. Vitalos makes no return-on-investment promises without evidence, so any value estimates are stated with their assumptions.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Opportunity Assessment / Start an AI Opportunity Assessment

entries.question: What is an AI Prototype Sprint, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: An AI Prototype Sprint tests your highest-value AI idea quickly, using real workflows and data where appropriate, and measures it against criteria agreed in advance. It suits organisations with a prioritised use case that need evidence of value and feasibility before committing to production investment.
entries.fullAnswer: The sprint answers one question: does the evidence justify building this properly? Vitalos AI & Data and Engineering build a bounded prototype, evaluate it against the agreed criteria and give you a clear recommendation, including known limitations and risks. A successful prototype is not automatically production-ready, and prototype fees do not include production hardening unless that is explicitly agreed. If the evidence is positive, the next step is Production: engineering, integration, security, monitoring and governance of the capability, followed by Managed AI once it is live. If the evidence is weak, stopping at this point protects your budget.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Prototype Sprint / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for an AI Prototype Sprint, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a named sponsor, the people who do the work today, and access to representative data or test cases, or agreement to use synthetic data. You receive a working prototype, evaluation findings against the agreed criteria, a recommendation on production investment, and a record of known limitations and risks.
entries.fullAnswer: Evaluation criteria are agreed before testing starts, so success is defined by your outcome rather than by how impressive a demonstration looks. Testing against real workflows shows whether the idea survives contact with daily work. Model, API and cloud usage costs are separated from professional fees or capped by agreement, so experimentation does not create a surprise bill. Data readiness or governance gaps found during the sprint are reported plainly, because they may need a workstream of their own before production. Production hardening, integration and live operation are not part of the sprint unless agreed in writing.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Prototype Sprint / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is a Custom Digital Product engagement, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Custom Digital Product is for organisations that need a new product, portal, workflow platform or application designed around measurable user and business outcomes. Vitalos Engineering and Experience design and build it for production. It suits teams with a clear objective and a product owner who can make decisions.
entries.fullAnswer: Typical examples are customer or supplier portals, operational web applications, workflow systems and digital services that must integrate with existing systems. If the problem, users or scope are not yet validated, Vitalos will recommend a Product Discovery first; if they are, engineering can start directly. The product is built in working, tested increments through controlled environments, then validated for function, security, performance and accessibility before release. After launch, you can run the product yourselves with a documented handover, or continue with Vitalos for continuous improvement or Managed Engineering & Application Care.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Custom Digital Product / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for a Custom Digital Product, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a product owner with authority over priorities and acceptance, requirements understood well enough to build or a discovery first, and access to the systems and data the product integrates with. You receive a production product, architecture records, automated tests, a release pipeline, runbooks and a handover.
entries.fullAnswer: The product owner role matters most. Decisions on priorities, trade-offs and acceptance need to come quickly, or delivery slows. We also need access to environments, interfaces and vendor documentation for any systems involved. In return, you get more than code. Deliverables include architecture and decision records, automated tests and a release pipeline, operational documentation and runbooks, and a transition either to your team or to ongoing support. Third-party licences and cloud consumption are kept visible as pass-through costs rather than hidden inside the fee.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Custom Digital Product / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is the Application Modernisation offer, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: The Application Modernisation offer modernises, replaces or progressively refactors ageing software to reduce technical constraint and improve maintainability, reliability and your ability to change. It suits technology leaders whose legacy application limits growth, integration or reliability, and which must keep running while it changes.
entries.fullAnswer: Where legacy complexity is material, work begins with an assessment or technical inception to establish architecture, dependencies and migration constraints. Vitalos Engineering and Consulting then agree a target architecture with you and modernise in stages, each with migration, testing and rollback planned. Pricing follows that staged risk: discovery first, then milestones or time and materials, rather than a whole-programme fixed price before the uncertainty is understood. Once modernised, the application can move to your own team with a documented handover, or to Managed Engineering & Application Care or platform operations with Vitalos.

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Application Modernisation, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a sponsor, a business owner, and access to source code, environments and the people who know the current system. You receive a modernised architecture and application, migration plans and records, improved test coverage and release pipeline, and updated documentation and runbooks.
entries.fullAnswer: The people who know the current system are often the scarcest resource, so we plan their time with you early. Their knowledge of edge cases, undocumented behaviour and business rules reduces migration risk considerably. During delivery, every stage has acceptance criteria, testing and a rollback plan, and data migrations include reconciliation where the data is financially or operationally important. Known limitations and remaining technical debt are recorded rather than hidden, so you know exactly what you are taking over at the end of each stage.

entries.question: What is the Systems Integration offer, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Systems Integration connects disconnected platforms, services and data flows so information moves reliably between them and manual handoffs disappear. It suits operations and technology leaders whose teams re-key data between systems, or whose processes depend on fragile manual transfers and spreadsheets.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos Engineering maps ownership, interfaces and failure modes across the systems involved, then builds integrations tested for failure handling, retries, duplicate prevention and the behaviour of external dependencies. Where several systems or unclear ownership are involved, a short discovery comes first, because multi-system integration is one of the cases where building straight away is risky. Work is usually priced through time and materials or milestones. The natural next steps are wider process automation, or managed engineering to monitor and maintain the integrations.

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Systems Integration, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a sponsor, a business owner, access to the systems, interfaces and vendor documentation involved, and contacts at any third-party suppliers. You receive integrated, automated workflows, interface and data-flow documentation, monitoring and alerting for integration failures, and runbooks for operating them.
entries.fullAnswer: Integrations fail at the edges, so Vitalos documents who owns each system, what each interface promises and what happens when something goes wrong. Monitoring and alerts tell your team, or ours, when a data flow stops or slows, rather than leaving users to discover it. Licence or API fees for third-party platforms are not included in the Vitalos fee and are kept visible. If a vendor's system or terms limit what can be integrated, we tell you early, because Vitalos cannot guarantee the behaviour of services it does not control.

entries.question: What is the Business Process Automation offer, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Business Process Automation redesigns manual, repetitive operations and automates them using workflow automation, systems integration and AI where each adds value. It suits operations leaders whose processes consume time, introduce errors and do not scale, and who want measurable improvement rather than another tool.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos Consulting, Engineering and AI & Data work together: first redesigning the process with the people who run it, then building the automation and integrations, then measuring the result against a baseline agreed at the start. Bounded, measurable workflows come first, before any broad automation. The automated process gets clear documentation and a named owner, so it does not become a black box. The natural next steps are managed automation, or extending the same approach to adjacent processes once the first one has proved its value.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Business Process Automation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Business Process Automation, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a sponsor, a business owner, and the people who run the process today, so the redesign reflects reality. You receive a redesigned workflow, automation and integrations in production, before-and-after measures agreed at the start, and documentation and ownership for the automated process.
entries.fullAnswer: The people doing the work know where the exceptions and workarounds are, and those details decide whether automation succeeds, so we ask for their time in short, focused sessions. Measures are agreed before work starts, such as time saved, cycle time or manual effort, so you can see whether the change worked. Vitalos will not automate a process that has not been redesigned first. Where AI forms part of the workflow, it is evaluated against agreed criteria and includes human review where the risk warrants it.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Business Process Automation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is the Data & BI Modernisation offer, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Data & BI Modernisation creates a usable data foundation and the reporting and decision systems built on it. It suits leaders who cannot trust their reporting, whose management information is assembled by hand, or whose data is too fragmented to support decisions or AI.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos AI & Data connects, cleans, models and governs the data needed for analytics and AI, then improves operational reporting, metrics and decision systems on that foundation. Important metrics get documented business definitions so that different reports stop giving different answers. Work is usually priced through milestones or time and materials. The natural next steps are AI implementation, once the data can support it, or managed data, where Vitalos operates pipelines and quality controls so the foundation stays reliable over time.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Data & BI Modernisation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Data & BI Modernisation, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a sponsor, owners for the main data sources, and access to the source systems and current reports. You receive a connected, governed data foundation, documented definitions for key metrics, modernised reporting and dashboards, and monitoring for data quality and pipeline failures.
entries.fullAnswer: Source owners matter because data quality problems are usually business problems as much as technical ones. They help agree definitions, resolve conflicts between systems and decide who can see what. Vitalos applies data controls throughout: lineage, quality expectations, schema management, access control and data minimisation, retention and deletion rules, and reconciliation where data is financially or operationally important. Data platform licences and cloud consumption are kept visible as pass-through costs rather than built silently into the fee. Definitions for key metrics are agreed with you and documented.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Data & BI Modernisation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Customer Experience Transformation, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Customer Experience Transformation improves the end-to-end customer digital journey and the processes and systems behind it. It suits digital, product and customer leaders whose journeys are fragmented, hard to use or disconnected from operations, and where that is costing adoption, conversion or service quality.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos Experience and Engineering review the journey for usability, accessibility and service friction, redesign it together with the operational workflow behind it, and set out how to implement the change. Redesigning screens without fixing the process behind them rarely lasts, so both are addressed together. Work usually starts with discovery and is then delivered in milestones. The natural next steps are product engineering to build the redesigned journey, followed by continuous optimisation once it is live. Accessibility is part of the review from the start, not an afterthought.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Customer Experience Transformation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Customer Experience Transformation, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a sponsor, a business owner, the teams who run the operations behind the journey, and access to customers or customer data for research where appropriate. You receive an evidence-based experience review, a redesigned customer journey, a prioritised improvement plan and an implementation roadmap.
entries.fullAnswer: Research with real customers, or analysis of how they actually use your services, keeps the redesign grounded in evidence rather than opinion. Where personal data is involved, purposes, access and retention are agreed before research starts. The review covers usability, accessibility and service friction. The redesign covers the journey and the operational workflow that supports it, so the change can actually be delivered. Visual redesign that is not connected to the underlying process is outside the scope of this offer.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Customer Experience Transformation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Engineering Rescue, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Engineering Rescue stabilises or completes a slow, unstable, unfinished or poorly engineered product, including systems built by another supplier. It starts with a paid rescue assessment that establishes a known technical baseline, then moves to controlled stabilisation and remediation. It suits organisations whose business depends on software that is failing them.
entries.fullAnswer: Typical triggers are a supplier exit, a key developer leaving, repeated incidents, a stalled project with money spent and little delivered, or a hard deadline the current system cannot meet. Vitalos does not take ownership of what it has not seen, so the assessment comes first: incident and risk triage, an estate and codebase review, and a prioritised recovery plan. Stabilisation and remediation follow in priority order, with each change reviewed, tested and reversible. Afterwards the system can return to your team with a handover, move to Managed Engineering & Application Care, or proceed to modernisation.

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Engineering Rescue, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide an executive sponsor who can decide quickly, administrative access to code, infrastructure, accounts and domains, and whatever documentation, incident history and supplier information exists. You receive a known technical baseline, a prioritised recovery plan, stabilisation and controlled remediation, and a recommendation on what should happen next.
entries.fullAnswer: Full access on day one matters in a rescue, because delays in access are delays in stabilisation. Vitalos also needs a single client contact for priorities and agreement to work through change control, so fixes do not collide with new requests. During remediation, release and environment control are restored, monitoring and backups are checked, and knowledge is documented as it is recovered. Vitalos will not offer a service-level commitment before the assessment is complete, and will not do work that requires bypassing legal, licensing or security obligations.

entries.question: What is Managed Engineering & Application Care, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Managed Engineering & Application Care gives live applications ongoing ownership and improvement: maintenance, defect fixes, updates, incident support and retained engineering capacity. It suits organisations that need continuity without a full internal product engineering team, or extra capacity alongside their own team.
entries.fullAnswer: There are two common shapes. Application Care covers maintenance, fixes, updates, incident support and planned technical improvement within an agreed service boundary. Retained engineering gives you reserved capacity that works with your own technology or product team against an improvement roadmap. Both are priced monthly and normally invoiced in advance, because capacity is reserved for you. For systems Vitalos did not build, a takeover assessment comes first. Over time the relationship can widen to further systems or services, but only where there is a genuine need.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Managed Engineering & Application Care / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Managed Engineering & Application Care, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide an agreed service boundary, named contacts, escalation routes and the access needed to operate the system, plus a takeover assessment for any system Vitalos did not build. You receive maintenance, fixes and updates within scope, incident support, monitoring coordination, an improvement backlog and regular service reviews.
entries.fullAnswer: The service boundary defines what is included, so there are no surprises about what counts as support and what counts as new work. Work outside the boundary is quoted separately. Monthly service reviews cover incidents, backlog, risks and improvements, and strategic accounts also get periodic value reviews focused on outcomes rather than ticket counts. Vitalos does not offer unlimited support, and will not commit to service levels for an inherited system until that system has been assessed. The boundary, contacts and escalation routes are written into the service schedule before the service starts.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Managed Engineering & Application Care / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Product Discovery, and who is it for?
entries.shortAnswer: Product Discovery defines a new product before major engineering investment. Vitalos Experience and Consulting validate the problem, the users, the key journeys and the scope, and set the prototype direction. It suits product and digital leaders whose idea is promising but unproven, and it usually leads to a Custom Digital Product.
entries.fullAnswer: Typical triggers are a planned digital proposition whose users and scope have not been validated, or a substantial redesign where the team is not yet sure what to build first. Building before those questions are answered wastes engineering investment, so discovery comes first and engineering starts from evidence rather than assumptions. Product Discovery is normally fixed-fee, because it is a bounded engagement. It sits within Digital Product Transformation, and the natural next step is a Custom Digital Product, followed by integration, analytics and continuous product improvement once the product is live. You can also take the results to your own team or to another supplier.

entries.question: What do we need to provide for Product Discovery, and what do we receive?
entries.shortAnswer: You provide a named sponsor, a business owner who can make decisions, and access to prospective or current users for research. You receive a validated problem and target users, the key user journeys, a defined scope and prototype direction, and a delivery backlog that engineering can start from.
entries.fullAnswer: Research with real users is the core of the engagement, so access to them, or to people who represent them, matters most. Where personal data is involved in research, purposes, access and retention are agreed before it starts. Vitalos also needs timely decisions on priorities and scope, because the backlog should reflect what you actually want to build. The outputs are designed to be used: whether Vitalos or another team builds the product, engineering can start from validated journeys and a scoped backlog rather than assumptions. Building the product is not part of Product Discovery; it follows as a Custom Digital Product.

entries.question: Which Vitalos solution fits our problem?
entries.shortAnswer: Start from the problem. Unclear AI value points to AI Transformation. Manual, fragmented operations point to Business Process Modernisation. A new or underperforming product points to Digital Product Transformation. Ageing systems point to Application Modernisation. Untrusted data points to Data & Intelligence Transformation. An unstable critical platform points to Technology Recovery & Reliability.
entries.fullAnswer: Solutions are how Vitalos organises several practices around one substantial business problem. Each solution page explains the signals that the problem is present, its business impact, the Vitalos approach, typical phases and the offers that work as starting points. Your situation may span more than one solution, which is common: operational modernisation often leads to integration, data and AI work, and the same accountable team can carry it forward. If none fits, or you are unsure, describe the problem in your own words and Talk to Vitalos. We will point you to the most sensible starting point, including telling you if Vitalos is not the right firm.

entries.question: What is AI Transformation, and when do we need it?
entries.shortAnswer: AI Transformation is for organisations under pressure to adopt AI but unclear on value, governance, data readiness or the route to production. Vitalos helps you choose the right use cases, prove them, put the strongest into secure production use and operate them, combining Consulting, AI & Data, Engineering and Managed Services.
entries.fullAnswer: Typical signals include scattered AI pilots that have not reached production, an unclear return on AI spend, important workflows that remain manual, uncertain data quality, and uncertainty about privacy, governance and human oversight. Without a prioritised route, effort spreads across disconnected experiments, and cost, reliability and vendor dependence surface only after commitments are made. Vitalos follows a staged path: assess, prioritise, prototype, move to production, scale and operate. Each stage has a decision gate, so you invest more only when the evidence justifies it. The usual starting point is an AI Opportunity Assessment.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Opportunity Assessment / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What are the stages of an AI Transformation, and where are the decision points?
entries.shortAnswer: An AI Transformation moves through assessment, prototype, production, scale and managed operation. Each stage ends with a decision: is there a use case worth testing, did the evidence justify production, is the system ready for controlled live use, where would wider adoption add value, and is the live service still delivering?
entries.fullAnswer: The stages follow the Vitalos AI journey: AI Opportunity Assessment > Prototype > Production > Managed AI, with scaling across workflows or teams once a capability has proved itself. The gates protect your investment. A prototype that impresses in a demonstration does not move to production unless it meets evaluation criteria agreed in advance. Production work adds integration, security, monitoring, human oversight and cost controls. Managed AI then keeps evaluating quality, risk and cost as models, data and usage change. You can stop or pause at any gate, and "not yet" is a legitimate result.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Opportunity Assessment / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Business Process Modernisation?
entries.shortAnswer: Business Process Modernisation is for organisations whose manual, slow or fragmented workflows limit growth or service. Vitalos maps how work happens today, redesigns the process, then uses software, integration, automation and AI where each helps, and measures the result against the starting point.
entries.fullAnswer: The signals are familiar: critical processes run on spreadsheets, the same data is re-keyed into several systems, handoffs cause delays and errors, and growth means adding people to the same manual steps. Consulting leads process discovery and redesign. Engineering builds and integrates the systems. AI & Data adds intelligent automation and operational intelligence. Experience makes the new workflow usable for the people who run it. Typical starting points are a Digital Transformation Discovery, Business Process Automation or Systems Integration, depending on how clear the problem already is.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Digital Transformation Discovery / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Will you simply automate our existing process?
entries.shortAnswer: No. Vitalos redesigns the process before automating it, so you do not end up with a faster version of a broken workflow. Steps that add no value are removed first. Software, integration, automation and AI then support the redesigned process, and agreed measures show whether it works better.
entries.fullAnswer: Automating a poor process locks in its problems. We start by understanding the work as it actually happens, including workarounds and exceptions, with the people who do it. The target workflow is agreed before technology is chosen. Deterministic workflow automation, systems integration and AI are then combined deliberately: rules-based automation where outcomes must be predictable, AI where judgement on unstructured information adds value. Integrations are tested for failure handling and retries before they carry live work, and ownership of the new process is agreed before the engagement ends.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Business Process Automation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Digital Product Transformation?
entries.shortAnswer: Digital Product Transformation is for organisations that need a new or substantially better digital product, such as a platform, portal, application, commerce experience or digital service. Vitalos combines Experience, Engineering and Consulting to discover, design, engineer, launch and keep improving a product that creates measurable value.
entries.fullAnswer: Common signals are a new proposition whose users and scope are not yet validated, an existing product with weak adoption, journeys fragmented across tools, a product that cannot change fast enough, or earlier build attempts that stalled. Building before the problem and users are understood wastes engineering investment, and products that cannot evolve after launch stagnate. Vitalos runs discovery, design and engineering as one engagement rather than as separate handoffs between suppliers. Typical offers are Product Discovery, Custom Digital Product and Customer Experience Transformation.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Custom Digital Product / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Can Vitalos take a digital product from idea to launch and beyond?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Vitalos can validate the problem and users, design the service and interface, engineer the product in tested increments, release it with security, performance and accessibility checks, and keep improving it after launch. You can also engage Vitalos for a single stage, such as discovery or build.
entries.fullAnswer: Product work follows a simple sequence: discover, design, engineer, launch and improve. Discovery validates the problem, users, journeys and scope. Design covers the service, the interface and the technical architecture. Engineering delivers working increments through controlled environments with peer review and automated checks. Launch includes validation for function, security, performance and accessibility, with rollback planned. After launch, you can take over with a documented handover, or keep Vitalos for continuous product improvement against an agreed roadmap. Outcome reviews then show whether the product is creating the value it was built for.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Custom Digital Product / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Application Modernisation?
entries.shortAnswer: Application Modernisation is for organisations whose ageing applications cost too much, carry too much risk, change too slowly or cannot integrate. Vitalos assesses the system, agrees a target architecture, then modernises, replaces or progressively refactors it in controlled stages, and can operate the result afterwards.
entries.fullAnswer: Signals include small changes that take months, systems only a few people understand, difficult integration with newer platforms, concerns about security patching or hosting, and maintenance absorbing the budget meant for improvement. Consulting leads the assessment and target architecture, Engineering migrates and refactors, and Managed Services takes over operation through a formal transition so the modernised system does not stagnate. The usual starting point is a Technology Health Assessment, followed by the Application Modernisation offer and, if you want ongoing support, Managed Engineering & Application Care.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Technology Health Assessment / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Do we have to replace our legacy system all at once?
entries.shortAnswer: No. Vitalos usually modernises in stages chosen by risk and value, so the business keeps running while the system changes. Depending on what the assessment finds, parts may be replaced, re-platformed or progressively refactored, each with migration, testing and rollback planned before work starts.
entries.fullAnswer: Big-bang replacements concentrate risk into a single cut-over. A staged approach lets you retire the riskiest or most costly parts first, prove the new architecture early and spread investment over time. Where legacy complexity is material, we start with an assessment of architecture, dependencies and migration constraints, because building without that knowledge is one of the risks discovery exists to prevent. Staged work is priced through milestones or time and materials rather than a whole-programme fixed price set before the uncertainty is understood, and we review the plan with you at each stage boundary.

entries.question: What is Data & Intelligence Transformation?
entries.shortAnswer: Data & Intelligence Transformation is for organisations whose data is fragmented, unreliable or not turning into decisions and AI capability. Vitalos connects, cleans, models and governs your data, then builds trusted reporting, metrics and decision systems on that foundation, adding analytics or AI once the foundation can support it.
entries.fullAnswer: Signals include reports that disagree, management information assembled by hand in spreadsheets, data spread across systems without agreed definitions or owners, and AI initiatives that stall because the data is not ready. AI & Data leads the work, Consulting ties it to the decisions the business needs to make, and Engineering integrates the source systems.
