Controls keep the foundation trustworthy: source ownership and lineage, quality expectations, schema management, access control, retention rules and documented business definitions for important metrics. The usual offer is Data & BI Modernisation.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Data & BI Modernisation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Do we need a new data platform before we can use AI?
entries.shortAnswer: Not necessarily. Vitalos first assesses your data sources, quality, ownership and the decisions the data should support. Sometimes connecting and governing existing sources is enough; sometimes a new platform is justified. AI work then builds on data that has owners, definitions and quality checks.
entries.fullAnswer: Many AI projects struggle because the data they depend on is fragmented or untrusted, not because the model is wrong. That does not always mean a large platform programme. The assessment shows the smallest credible route: perhaps integrating a few key systems and agreeing definitions for the metrics that matter, perhaps a modern data platform. Good reporting has value on its own, and it also creates the base that later AI work needs. When data readiness is the real blocker in an AI conversation, Vitalos will say so and recommend fixing the data first.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Data & BI Modernisation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What is Technology Recovery & Reliability, and when do we need it?
entries.shortAnswer: Technology Recovery & Reliability is for organisations whose critical platform is unstable, slow or unfinished, for example after a supplier or key developer has left. Vitalos triages the immediate risk, assesses the system to establish a known baseline, stabilises and remediates it in priority order, then operates it or hands it back.
entries.fullAnswer: Typical signals are frequent or hard-to-diagnose incidents, a stalled project with money spent and little delivered, performance degrading as use grows, an original supplier or team that is no longer available, and nobody able to say with confidence what is safe to change. An unstable critical platform disrupts operations and customers, consumes the people who keep it running and blocks every improvement that depends on it. Engineering leads the work with Managed Services, and Consulting joins where needed. The usual offers are Engineering Rescue, a Technology Health Assessment where the problem is risk rather than active failure, and Managed Engineering & Application Care once the system is stable.

entries.question: How does a Technology Recovery & Reliability engagement work?
entries.shortAnswer: A Technology Recovery & Reliability engagement moves through five stages: triage, assessment, stabilisation, remediation and operation. Vitalos does not promise outcomes before the assessment; it establishes what is wrong first, and recovery, modernisation or replacement are all legitimate conclusions, chosen on evidence.
entries.fullAnswer: Triage protects what the business depends on today. The assessment then establishes a known baseline across architecture, code quality, security posture, operations, ownership and documentation. Stabilisation tackles the causes of instability that matter most, and remediation works through a prioritised recovery plan, with each change reviewed, tested and reversible. Before taking on ongoing operational responsibility, Vitalos completes its acceptance assessment for inherited systems, and it will say so if the risk, access or legality makes responsible support impossible. Once stable, the system moves into managed engineering or application care within a defined service boundary, or back to your own team with a documented handover.

entries.question: Is Vitalos Cyber Essentials certified?
entries.shortAnswer: Not yet. Vitalos is preparing for Cyber Essentials under the current NCSC requirements, version 3.3, and its internal security architecture is designed around the scheme's five controls: firewalls, secure configuration, security update management, user access control and malware protection. Vitalos will list the certificate only once it is held.
entries.fullAnswer: The Vitalos approach is to make the controls real first and certify second, because a certificate only means something when everyday behaviour matches it. Vitalos has carried out an internal gap assessment against version 3.3 to plan the work needed before applying. Cyber Essentials Plus, which adds independent technical testing of the same controls, is the next step when public sector, NHS or enterprise work calls for it. Until a certificate is issued, Vitalos will not display badges or describe itself as certified, and procurement answers will state its status accurately.

entries.question: Is Vitalos ISO 27001 certified?
entries.shortAnswer: No. Vitalos is not ISO/IEC 27001 certified. Its internal security standard is being built to align to ISO 27001 practices, such as asset inventory, access management, supplier management, incident management, backup and recovery and risk ownership, and Vitalos will pursue certification when client demand justifies it.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos follows a deliberate sequence: build working controls, document them, measure them, then have them validated independently. Cyber Essentials comes first, then Cyber Essentials Plus where independent testing helps, then ISO 27001 readiness and certification when the enterprise pipeline justifies the cost and the ongoing audit burden. Formal management system elements, such as a statement of applicability, internal audits and management review, will be added as that readiness matures. Vitalos will never describe itself as "ISO compliant" as a substitute for certification.

entries.question: What is Vitalos's approach to UK GDPR?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos treats data protection as an operating control, not a registration badge. For each engagement it identifies whether it acts as controller or processor, puts a data processing agreement in place where it processes personal data for you, uses impact assessments for higher-risk processing, and handles personal data only for defined purposes.
entries.fullAnswer: Where delivery involves personal data, Vitalos makes its purposes, collection, access, retention, third-party processing and deletion visible from the start, rather than leaving them to be discovered at release. Data minimisation and access control are part of design, and retention and deletion rules are set for the data each system holds. Legal interpretation is escalated to qualified advisers, because engineering judgement does not replace legal advice. Vitalos also tracks changes to the UK framework, including the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, whose data protection provisions were in force by June 2026.

entries.question: Will Vitalos sign a data processing agreement?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Whenever Vitalos processes personal data on your behalf, it puts in place a written data processing agreement that meets UK GDPR Article 28, covering purpose, data types, your instructions, security, subprocessors, help with rights requests and breaches, deletion or return at the end, audit and international transfers.
entries.fullAnswer: A confidentiality clause is not a substitute for a data processing agreement, and Vitalos does not treat it as one. Vitalos can work with your data processing agreement or provide its own. Roles are described accurately: Vitalos may be your processor for service data while acting as an independent controller for its own records, such as billing, account contacts, security and legal records, and the agreement reflects that rather than forcing a single label. Where a restricted international transfer is involved, the agreement records the safeguard used and the transfer assessment.

entries.question: Is Vitalos a data controller or a data processor?
entries.shortAnswer: It depends on the activity. When Vitalos processes personal data on your instructions to deliver a service, it normally acts as your processor. For its own business records, such as billing, contacts, security logs and website enquiries, it acts as controller. Each engagement records the roles accurately before any data is shared.
entries.fullAnswer: Getting roles right matters because the obligations follow them. Vitalos assesses the controller and processor roles for each engagement before drafting privacy terms, rather than copying a template. Where Vitalos is your processor, it acts only on your documented instructions, and a data processing agreement applies. For data collected through its website, Vitalos Technologies Limited is the controller, as its privacy notice explains. Where the roles are not clear-cut, legal interpretation is confirmed with qualified advisers rather than assumed. The agreed roles are written into the contract before any personal data is shared.

entries.question: Which third parties process personal data sent through the Vitalos website?
entries.shortAnswer: For enquiries sent through its website, Vitalos uses four service providers: Vercel for hosting, Supabase for the database, Resend for email delivery and Cloudflare for bot protection. Vitalos does not sell personal data, and where these providers process data outside the UK, recognised safeguards apply.
entries.fullAnswer: The Vitalos website privacy notice, version 2026-10, explains how enquiries are handled. Vitalos collects your name, organisation, work email, optional role, what you are trying to achieve, your timeframe, an optional budget range, the page you enquired from and any campaign tags in the link you followed. A one-way hash of your IP address is stored to protect the form from abuse. Where providers process data outside the UK, including in the United States, the transfer is protected by UK adequacy regulations or the UK International Data Transfer Addendum. Subprocessors for client engagements are agreed separately, in each data processing agreement.

entries.question: Will you tell us which subprocessors handle our project data?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Where Vitalos processes personal data for you, subprocessors are authorised in your data processing agreement, either specifically or under a general authorisation with advance notice of changes and a right to object. Each subprocessor is bound by equivalent data protection terms, and Vitalos remains responsible to you for them.
entries.fullAnswer: The Vitalos standard is to keep a register of the providers it uses to process client data, recording the provider, purpose, data categories, location and transfer safeguards, security evidence and the Vitalos owner, which gives your privacy team what it needs to approve the arrangement. If you require specific approval for particular high-risk providers, Vitalos can accommodate that. Vitalos will not accept an outright ban on subprocessors where that would be inconsistent with how the service has to be delivered, but it will explain why openly and look for an alternative that works.

entries.question: How will Vitalos access our systems, and how is that access controlled?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos asks only for the access each role needs. Access to your systems is named to individuals, uses the least privilege necessary, is reviewed during the engagement, and is removed or transferred promptly when no longer needed. Vitalos does not use shared logins for your systems, and credentials are never passed around in chat or email.
entries.fullAnswer: Where practical, production systems for long-lived solutions stay in accounts you own, with Vitalos given named, revocable access. Each client's code repositories, documents, secrets and access groups are kept separate from other clients', and one client's data is never used as test data for another. Machine access for deployment pipelines uses dedicated service identities or federated credentials rather than personal tokens. At the end of an engagement, removing or transferring access is part of the closure checklist, and, wherever possible, the Vitalos person approving access is not the person requesting it.

entries.question: How does Vitalos classify and handle our data?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos uses four data classes: Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted. Client documents, contracts, source code and commercial data are Confidential. Credentials, production secrets, security findings, regulated datasets and highly sensitive personal data are Restricted, with need-to-know access, strong authentication and dedicated, controlled storage.
entries.fullAnswer: Classification decides where data can be stored, how it is shared, which devices can access it and which AI tools may process it. Confidential information is shared with named people rather than through anonymous public links, and guest access is reviewed when a project closes. Restricted information is shared only through approved, controlled channels, and browser-only or managed-device access may be required. The model is applied through clear defaults and dedicated locations rather than asking people to label every document by hand, because a scheme nobody follows is not a control.

entries.question: How do we report a security vulnerability or concern?
entries.shortAnswer: Report security vulnerabilities or concerns to Vitalos at support@vitalos.co.uk, marking the message as a security report. That address is the Vitalos security contact. Include enough detail to understand the issue, the systems affected and how to reach you, and Vitalos will route the report to the person responsible.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos handles security reports through its security incident procedure, which records the issue, the systems and people affected, containment actions, decisions and follow-up, and ends with a review of lessons learned. Reports that concern client systems Vitalos operates are shared with the affected client under the incident process in that client's contract. A security.txt file will be published once someone is accountable for monitoring the disclosure route, so that researchers can find the right contact automatically. Until then, support@vitalos.co.uk is the single route for security reports, so please send them there rather than to individuals.

entries.question: Will Vitalos complete our security questionnaire?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Send security and supplier questionnaires through the procurement route on the Vitalos contact page. Answers reflect what actually exists today, with evidence where it can be shared, and Vitalos will say plainly where a control is planned rather than in place, instead of giving a vague answer.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos builds an approved answer library as questionnaires arrive, so answers stay consistent, are linked to evidence and are reviewed before they go out of date. Sensitive evidence, such as full policies, insurance certificates or assessment summaries, is shared under appropriate confidentiality rather than published. Vitalos treats questionnaire answers as commitments, not marketing, so they are checked by the person who owns the evidence. If your questionnaire raises requirements Vitalos does not yet meet, it will tell you, explain any plan to meet them and, where needed, adjust scope or price for the extra work.

entries.question: Does Vitalos carry out penetration testing?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos does not offer penetration testing as its own service. Where your project needs a penetration test or formal security audit, Vitalos scopes it separately, uses a qualified specialist provider or coordinates with yours, and then fixes the findings as part of the engineering work.
entries.fullAnswer: Penetration testing needs qualified, independent capability, and Vitalos will not market it until it genuinely has that. Security in Vitalos delivery comes from design reviews, secure development practices, dependency scanning, release security gates and access controls; independent testing then adds external evidence on top. When a penetration test is needed, for example before launching a public service or to satisfy a client or regulator, Vitalos plans it into the timeline, works with the testing provider and remediates findings according to their severity. The security observations in a Technology Health Assessment are not a penetration test.

entries.question: How would Vitalos tell us about a data breach?
entries.shortAnswer: Your contract defines what counts as a security incident or personal data breach, how and when Vitalos notifies you, what information it provides and how updates follow. Vitalos notifies promptly with the facts available, then keeps you updated as the investigation continues, rather than waiting for a complete picture.
entries.fullAnswer: Breach handling has to work under pressure, so roles are agreed in advance. The contract sets out the notification route and contact, notification timing appropriate to Vitalos's role and your regulatory obligations, the initial information required, the update rhythm, cooperation and evidence, responsibility for root-cause analysis and remediation, who communicates with regulators and affected individuals, and how costs are allocated where one party caused the breach. Vitalos avoids promising complete forensic detail within a few hours, because facts may not yet exist; it promises prompt, honest notification and steady updates.

entries.question: Do you vet the people who work on our project?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes. Vitalos applies risk-based checks appropriate to each role and client, including right-to-work checks where the law requires them and references where relevant. Everyone working on your project, including contractors, signs confidentiality, data protection and IP terms and must complete Vitalos security onboarding before getting access.
entries.fullAnswer: If your environment requires specific screening, such as BPSS or similar checks, tell Vitalos at the start so it can confirm whether it can staff the work accordingly; any such requirement is written into the security schedule. Access follows least privilege and is removed promptly when no longer needed. Contractor performance and compliance with Vitalos standards are reviewed as part of delivery quality, and critical knowledge is never left with one person. Contractor onboarding is shorter than employee onboarding, but security, access, confidentiality, delivery standards and escalation are mandatory for everyone.

entries.question: What personal data does the Vitalos website collect, and how long is it kept?
entries.shortAnswer: When you send an enquiry, Vitalos collects your name, organisation, work email, optional role, what you are trying to achieve, your timeframe, an optional budget range and the page you enquired from. Enquiries are kept for 24 months after the last contact and then deleted. You are not added to marketing lists.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos Technologies Limited is the controller of this data, and its lawful basis is its legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries and keeping its website secure. To protect the form from abuse, a one-way hash of your IP address is stored, and Cloudflare Turnstile checks that the enquiry is not from a bot. The website does not use analytics or advertising cookies. If an enquiry leads to working together, the relevant details are kept for as long as that relationship and legal obligations require. You can ask to access, correct or delete your data by emailing support@vitalos.co.uk, and you can complain to the ICO.

entries.question: What is the Vitalos Trust Centre?
entries.shortAnswer: The Vitalos Trust Centre is where buyers check how Vitalos approaches security, privacy, Responsible AI, accessibility and resilience, which certifications it actually holds, and how to request controlled procurement evidence. It shows only controls and claims that exist, with review dates, and never lists certifications as coming soon.
entries.fullAnswer: Trust should be verifiable, so the Trust Centre follows the Vitalos evidence-before-claims policy: each trust item has an owner, an evidence location and a review date. Public pages give summaries and current status. Sensitive material, such as full policies, insurance certificates or assessment results, is available through a controlled request route rather than published. The Trust Centre will grow as the evidence grows, for example when Cyber Essentials is achieved or a subprocessor list for client services is published. A smaller, truthful Trust Centre is more useful to you than a polished page of empty badges.

entries.question: Why doesn't Vitalos show client logos?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos shows a client's name or logo only with that client's explicit permission, and only for work Vitalos actually delivered. It never uses invented logos, borrowed client lists or partner badges it has not earned. A short, truthful credibility strip is more useful to you than a crowded logo wall.
entries.fullAnswer: Logo walls are easy to fake and hard to verify, which is why many buyers discount them. Vitalos follows an evidence-before-claims policy: every public claim needs an owner and a source, confidentiality is not treated as marketing permission, and case-study rights are agreed at contracting time rather than assumed. As permissioned client work accumulates, names and outcomes will appear on the website alongside the evidence. Until then, Vitalos would rather leave a space empty than fill it with something misleading.

entries.question: How do you separate the founder's past experience from Vitalos's own track record?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos labels experience gained before the company existed as prior experience, never as Vitalos client work. Case studies, references and claims on the website and in proposals refer only to work contracted by Vitalos, unless they are clearly marked as earlier leadership or team experience.
entries.fullAnswer: This distinction protects you. Prior experience can be relevant and valuable, and it helps explain why Vitalos's people can do the work, but you should be able to tell the difference between what the founder or team did in earlier roles and what Vitalos has delivered as a company. Vitalos applies the same rule to its people's credentials and to any examples used in sales materials, and every proof asset is checked against that rule before it is used. If you are unsure which category a claim falls into, ask, and Vitalos will tell you.

entries.question: Will Vitalos use our name or project in its marketing?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos uses a client's name, logo, quote or project details in its marketing only with explicit permission. Confidentiality is not marketing consent, so Vitalos asks separately, usually through an optional clause in the statement of work. You can decline, agree to an anonymised case study, or agree to a named one.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos considers publicity at contracting time so that it is not chased months later, but the decision is always yours. If you agree, Vitalos shares the draft with you for approval, including any metrics, screenshots or architecture details, and anything sensitive is removed. Anonymised case studies still need your agreement and must be specific enough to be credible without identifying you. Vitalos may ask for publicity rights in exchange for a commercial concession, but that is always explicit, never assumed.

entries.question: How are Vitalos services organised?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos organises its services in three layers. Practices are the capabilities: Consulting, Engineering, AI & Data, Experience and Managed Services. Solutions are the business problems Vitalos solves across practices. Offers are bounded engagements you can buy, such as an AI Opportunity Assessment. Vitalos Labs sits alongside them as a separate capability.
entries.fullAnswer: The layers let you start from whichever direction makes sense to you. If you know your problem, start with a Solution: AI Transformation, Business Process Modernisation, Digital Product Transformation, Application Modernisation, Data & Intelligence Transformation or Technology Recovery & Reliability. If you know what you want to buy, go to the Offers, which explain who each one suits, what you receive, what we need from you and what comes next. If you are assessing capability, the practice pages explain each discipline, and Vitalos Labs shows research and technical proof, clearly labelled so it is never mistaken for client work. Behind all of this sits one delivery model and one accountable Engagement Lead, so you never have to coordinate separate Vitalos departments yourself.

entries.question: Will we have to coordinate several Vitalos teams?
entries.shortAnswer: No. However many practices contribute, you work with one integrated Vitalos team led by one named Engagement Lead. That person owns the outcome, scope, delivery health, commercial position, risks and reporting. Coordinating Consulting, Engineering, AI & Data, Experience and Managed Services is the responsibility of Vitalos, not yours.
entries.fullAnswer: Many problems cross disciplines. A process modernisation might need consulting, engineering, AI and experience design at the same time. Rather than splitting that across separate contracts, Vitalos assembles one team around your problem and gives it a single accountable lead. Specialists join and leave as the work needs them, but the lead, the plan and the reporting stay constant. The Engagement Lead works alongside a Technical Lead or Solution Architect who is authoritative on technical integrity, so both delivery and engineering judgement are covered. On your side, we ask for a named sponsor and a business owner who can make decisions and accept outcomes.

entries.question: What does Vitalos Consulting do?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Consulting helps you decide what should change, why it matters and how technology, data and AI should support it. Typical work includes technology strategy, digital transformation, AI strategy and adoption, technology assessments, architecture, operating model design, process transformation, roadmaps, technology due diligence and programme set-up.
entries.fullAnswer: Consulting is often the front door to larger change, but it is not separated from delivery. Vitalos consultants work close enough to engineering and operations that their recommendations survive implementation. Common starting points are a Digital Transformation Discovery, a Technology Health Assessment or an AI Opportunity Assessment. Each is bounded, normally fixed-fee, and ends with clear decisions: what to do next, why, in what order, with which dependencies and how success will be measured. You can take those recommendations forward with Vitalos, with another supplier or with your own team.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Digital Transformation Discovery / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Will your consulting end in a report that sits on a shelf?
entries.shortAnswer: A Vitalos consulting engagement should never end in a report that sits on a shelf. Every advisory engagement must end with decisions you can act on: what to do next, why, in what order, with what dependencies and how success will be measured. Consultants work closely with engineers, so recommendations reflect real constraints.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos judges consulting by whether it changes what you do. A Vitalos roadmap names priorities, sequencing, dependencies, risks and decision points, and where useful it defines a first phase precisely enough to estimate and contract. We avoid long documents that exist only to look thorough. If the evidence says you should not make an investment, or that Vitalos should not be the one to implement it, the recommendation will say so. Implementation with Vitalos is an option, never a condition of the advice.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Digital Transformation Discovery / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: What does Vitalos Engineering build?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Engineering designs, builds, integrates and modernises production software and platforms. That includes new digital products and portals, application modernisation, platform and cloud engineering, API and systems integration, quality and reliability engineering, performance work, and engineering rescue for systems that are unstable or unfinished.
entries.fullAnswer: Engineering is the technical execution core of Vitalos. It can take work directly from you when the requirement is clear, or pick it up after a discovery led by Consulting, AI & Data or Experience. The practice aims to be known for strong architecture, pragmatic implementation, production readiness, documentation, testing, security awareness and clean operational handover. Two rules guide it: fast must never mean careless, and enterprise must never mean unnecessarily complicated. Typical offers are Custom Digital Product, Application Modernisation, Systems Integration and Engineering Rescue.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Custom Digital Product / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Can we go straight to engineering without a discovery phase?
entries.shortAnswer: Yes, when the need is clear. If your objective, requirements, technical constraints, decision-makers and integrations are understood well enough, Vitalos can start engineering directly. Vitalos does not invent discovery phases to create billable steps, and recommends one only when skipping it would put your outcome at real risk.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos has two legitimate entry routes, consulting-led and engineering-led, and both follow the same governance and quality standards. Direct engineering usually starts with a short technical confirmation, then design, build, validation and release. We ask for paid discovery first when building straight away would create material risk: an unclear problem, complex legacy dependencies, sensitive or regulated data, AI use with uncertain data, several systems to integrate, a major transformation, or taking over an unstable system built by someone else. If the risk of building the wrong thing becomes clear during engineering, our engineering leads are expected to pause and raise it with you.

entries.question: What does Vitalos AI & Data do?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos AI & Data designs, builds, evaluates and operates AI and data capabilities. The work covers AI strategy, generative AI, AI agents, machine learning, intelligent automation, data engineering and platforms, analytics and business intelligence, enterprise AI integration, AI and data governance, model operations and data quality.
entries.fullAnswer: The practice exists to move AI beyond experiments into governed production use, and it avoids selling isolated chatbots without integration, governance or measurable outcomes. Engagements often follow the Vitalos AI journey: AI Opportunity Assessment > Prototype > Production > Managed AI. Data work matters as much as models, because many AI initiatives stall when data is fragmented or of poor quality, so the practice also builds data foundations, reporting and decision systems. Production AI is delivered with evaluation criteria, monitoring, security controls, cost tracking and human oversight appropriate to the use case.
entries.linkedOfferCta: AI Opportunity Assessment / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Is AI handled only by the AI & Data practice?
entries.shortAnswer: No. AI & Data is the specialist practice, but AI runs across the whole of Vitalos. Consulting covers AI strategy, business cases and governance. Engineering builds AI-enabled products and integrations. Experience designs how people interact with AI. Managed Services monitors, evaluates and improves live AI systems.
entries.fullAnswer: Treating AI as a capability across the firm means it is considered wherever it could help, and governed the same way everywhere. A process modernisation might include intelligent automation; a customer portal might include intelligent search; a managed service might include ongoing evaluation and cost optimisation of a live AI feature. The AI & Data practice sets the specialist methods for evaluation, data quality and model risk, and the other practices apply them. For you, this means one consistent approach to AI risk rather than different rules depending on which team happens to be involved.

entries.question: What does Vitalos Experience do?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Experience shapes how customers, employees and partners use your digital services. It covers digital product strategy, product discovery, user research, service design, UX and UI design, design systems, customer and commerce experience, accessibility, content and interaction design, and internal tools for employees.
entries.fullAnswer: Experience is not a standalone graphic design department. Its job is to connect user needs, service design, product strategy and engineering so that technology is useful, understandable and actually adopted. Typical work includes Product Discovery before major engineering investment, Customer Experience Transformation for fragmented digital journeys, and design system programmes that make delivery consistent and accessible. Experience work usually connects to engineering or a measurable implementation plan, and designers work within your technology, operational and commercial constraints. Accessibility is treated as part of design quality from the first sketch, not as an audit after launch.
entries.linkedOfferCta: Customer Experience Transformation / Talk to Vitalos

entries.question: Will you design something we cannot build or run?
entries.shortAnswer: That is exactly what Vitalos Experience is set up to avoid. Designers work alongside engineers and keep your operational and commercial constraints in view, so prototypes and journeys can actually be delivered. Experience work usually connects directly to engineering or to a measurable implementation plan.
entries.fullAnswer: Beautiful prototypes that cannot be built within your systems, budget or operating model waste money and goodwill. Vitalos designers check feasibility with engineering as they go, consider the processes behind each screen, and design for accessibility from the start. When a redesign depends on changes to underlying workflows or systems, we say so and include those changes in the plan. The outputs are designed to be implemented: validated journeys, a scoped backlog, design system components and acceptance criteria that engineering can work from, whether Vitalos or another team builds them.

entries.question: What does Vitalos Managed Services cover?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Managed Services takes ongoing responsibility for live systems. It covers application care, retained engineering capacity, platform and cloud operations, monitoring and incident management, release support, managed data, managed AI and continuous improvement, within an agreed service boundary, for systems Vitalos built or has responsibly taken over.
entries.fullAnswer: Managed Services turns a finished project into a supported, improving system. Each service has a defined scope, contacts, escalation routes, monitoring, runbooks and an improvement backlog, reviewed with you regularly. Operational commitments create real obligations, so Vitalos enters them carefully: a project moves into managed service only through a formal service transition, and for systems built by others we complete a takeover assessment first. We will not accept a service level for a system we have not been allowed to understand.

entries.question: How does Vitalos Labs relate to the five practices?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos Labs is separate from the five practices. It is the research and technical proof capability of Vitalos: it builds reference architectures, prototypes, evaluation methods and reusable engineering accelerators that the practices can use. Every Labs asset carries a maturity label, so a prototype is never presented as a supported product or as client work.
entries.fullAnswer: The five practices own Vitalos's client-facing capability, and Labs supports them. Labs exists to build reusable capability, demonstrate engineering judgement and explore technology before demand becomes mainstream. Its accelerators, such as assessment frameworks, code templates or reusable AI evaluation tooling, can make client delivery faster and more consistent. Labs is kept separate from client proof: the Work section is reserved for real client outcomes, while Labs shows research and experiments with clear status labels such as Research, Concept, Prototype or Accelerator. Labs is deliberately small and evidence-led. Most ideas stop before becoming products, and product investment only follows proven, repeated demand.

entries.question: Do you provide cloud and cyber security services?
entries.shortAnswer: Cloud engineering and operations sit within Vitalos Engineering and Managed Services, and security is built into everything Vitalos designs and delivers. Vitalos does not market specialist cyber services such as penetration testing or 24/7 security monitoring; where those are needed, it works with qualified specialists or your chosen provider.
entries.fullAnswer: You get cloud and platform engineering, deployment pipelines, observability and platform operations as part of our engineering and managed service work. Security is embedded through design reviews, secure development practices, release gates and access controls. We are deliberately careful about cyber claims: specialist assurance such as penetration testing, a security operations centre or round-the-clock monitoring needs qualified capability and an operating model that we will not imply before it exists. When your project needs that assurance, we tell you, scope it separately and bring in an appropriately qualified specialist, or coordinate with your own provider.

entries.question: Do you implement platforms such as Salesforce, SAP or ServiceNow?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos does not present itself as an implementation specialist for major enterprise platforms such as SAP, Salesforce or ServiceNow. Vitalos can integrate custom software and data with platforms like these where the scope allows, and will tell you plainly when a certified platform specialist is the better choice.
entries.fullAnswer: The Vitalos rule is to claim only capability it can demonstrate. Deep configuration of large enterprise platforms usually needs certified specialists and formal programme status, which Vitalos does not claim. What we do offer is the engineering around those platforms: integrating them with your other systems, building the workflows and data flows that connect them, and modernising applications that depend on them. Where a platform specialist is needed, we can work alongside them under a clear responsibility model, so you always know who is accountable for what.

entries.question: Do you build websites?
entries.shortAnswer: Vitalos builds web platforms, customer and supplier portals, commerce, operational web applications and digital products, especially where integration, data or AI is involved. Routine low-value brochure websites are generally not part of what Vitalos offers, unless there is a clear strategic reason to take the work on.
entries.fullAnswer: Vitalos is capable of building websites, but it does not want to be known primarily as a website company. Web work fits when it is part of something bigger: a platform that must integrate with your systems, a portal that changes how customers or staff work, a commerce operation, or a strategically important site within a broader transformation. If you are unsure which side of that line your project sits on, describe what the site needs to do and we will tell you honestly whether Vitalos is the right fit.
